Examples

hello_sim — server authority and client prediction

1 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

This version of examples/hello_net lets the server settle movement while clients predict their own square locally. Kit's simulation lane schedules fixed ticks and retains the history needed for correction. The conversion makes five changes, following the promotion checklist:

  1. Retag simulated state from owner to predict.
  2. Move frame-rate movement into a fixed-tick @(gd_tick) procedure.
  3. Declare safe input ranges with @(gd_input).
  4. Sample device input with @(gd_sample).
  5. Attach the lane through the generated network facade.

See docs/kit/quickstart-sim.md for the walkthrough.

Shell
bash build/build_scripts.sh examples/hello_sim
$GODOT --path examples/hello_sim &                      # window 1: Host
HELLO_LATENCY=120 $GODOT --path examples/hello_sim      # window 2: Join and compare prediction

Under the injected latency, your own square responds through local prediction. The remote square is displayed from delayed authority history (the watched view). HELLO_ROLE=serve $GODOT --headless --path examples/hello_sim runs the dedicated, avatarless authority. The role selects .Dedicated_Competitive; the normal Host path uses .Listen_Server_Action, with the same simulation code. bash examples/hello_sim/run.sh checks both profiles headless through generated read-only probes.
